look_here_first: Look for leathery evergreen foliage: alternate compound leaves usually have only 5–9 thick, smooth-edged leaflets that are glossy dark green above.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: evergreen to semi-evergreen large shrub or small tree

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: odd-pinnate leaves usually with only 5–9 thick leathery leaflets

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaflets entire and glossy dark green above

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flattened red drupes are covered with red hairs

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Evergreen to semi-evergreen shrub or small tree.

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Usually 5–9 thick leathery entire leaflets; glossy dark green above, duller beneath.

key_traits.label: Stem
key_traits.text: Young rachises and stems often reddish.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Compact branched clusters of small creamy-white flowers.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Flattened red drupes with red hairs.

key_traits.text: Joey Santore's West Texas pinyon-pine video includes an exact Rhus virens flowering branch frame showing inflorescence plus compound-leaf context.
